title: The Sweet Vow
premise: Juniper Oyelaran inherited her late father's debt-ridden vineyard on a small island where the last ferry of the season marks the boundary between belonging and escape. To survive a family reunion without pitying questions, she hires Theo Marchetti, a quiet ferry mechanic with his own buried grievance against the island's most powerful family, to pose as her boyfriend. Their fake romance deepens into something real even as Juniper uncovers evidence that the loan strangling her vineyard was engineered through fraud, forcing her to choose between a safe, invisible settlement and public justice that could cost her everything. In the end, she testifies, saves the vineyard on her own terms, and boards the last ferry not to flee but to bring Theo home.
about_author: Sable Reyes is the pen name of a former sommelier who spent five years working harvest seasons on a coastal island before turning to fiction. Her novels blend slow-burn romance with stories of small communities reckoning quietly with their own injustices.

chapters.title: Debts Instead of Grapes
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She surveys the failing vineyard, a foreclosure notice pinned beside her father's photograph, and rehearses the lie she'll tell at Sunday's family reunion: that her life is fine. The emotional beat is weary self-containment; she treats her heart like a muscle she has trained not to feel.

chapters.title: The Ferry Mechanic
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At the dock she watches Theo Marchetti repair an engine with patient hands and no small talk, and impulsively asks him to be her date for the reunion. He refuses twice, then names a price: help clearing out his late mother's boathouse. The beat is reluctant bargain.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Over coffee they draft terms: no real names to his past, no questions about her father's debts, nothing after the last ferry in October. Juniper signs the napkin like a contract. The beat is guarded humor masking two people who have both been burned by this town.

chapters.title: Reunion
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The Oyelaran reunion brims with cousins, casseroles, and her aunt's surgical questions about money. Theo plays his role so well—remembering details, deflecting pity—that Juniper forgets it's a performance until their hands link under the table. The beat is the first crack in her armor.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Dessert turns tender when Juniper defends him from a snide remark about 'dock rats,' and afterward they sit on the seawall saying true things by accident. Both retreat fast, but neither can unhear it. The beat is warmth followed by mutual panic.

chapters.title: The Boathouse
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Clearing Theo's mother's boathouse, Juniper finds letters suggesting his mother was cheated out of waterfront land decades ago—by the same family whose bank now holds Juniper's loan. The beat is discovery; the fake plot acquires stakes beyond romance.

chapters.title: Harvest Hands
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo shows up unasked to help with the grape harvest, and the crew adopts him as one of their own. Juniper catches herself planning around his presence. The beat is belonging sneaking up on someone who swore off it.

chapters.title: The Calloway Ledger
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Following the land trail, Theo confronts old family friend Margaret Calloway, who admits the Marchetti property was taken through forged signatures but begs him to let sleeping dogs lie. The beat is anger tempered by fear of what truth costs.

chapters.title: Storm Season
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A storm threatens the harvest; Juniper and Theo work all night tying vines, soaked and laughing, and nearly kiss before lightning splits the silence. She pulls back, citing the rules. The beat is desire colliding with self-protection.

chapters.title: What the Bank Knew
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Digging for her own loan documents, Juniper finds irregularities: her father's signature dated weeks after his death. The loan that ruined her was manufactured. The beat is grief transmuting into fury.

chapters.title: Two Frauds, One Table
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They compare evidence over takeout and realize the same man—bank officer Dale Voss—forged both families' papers. For the first time, the fake relationship feels like the only honest thing between them. The beat is alliance deepening into intimacy.

chapters.title: The Almost
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. After a town meeting where Voss smiles and shakes hands, Theo walks Juniper home and this time the kiss happens. Morning brings Juniper's cold withdrawal: this wasn't the deal. The beat is joy curdling into the story's first real heartbreak.

chapters.title: Lending Pieces
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper confesses to her aunt why she keeps everyone at arm's length: her father borrowed against everything they loved and died leaving her the wreckage. Loving people, she learned, means losing them solvent. The beat is vulnerability offered too late.

chapters.title: Voss Makes His Move
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Voss offers Theo hush money and a job off-island, hinting he'll call Juniper's loan due within thirty days if anyone talks. Theo pretends to consider. The beat is rising menace; the antagonist stops being abstract.

chapters.title: The Settlement Offer
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A lawyer delivers an offer: sign away the vineyard cheaply, receive forgiveness of debt, say nothing. It would make her invisible again—safe, broke, free. The beat is temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: Broken Terms
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Juniper accuses Theo of taking Voss's deal; Theo, hurt, produces the untouched check. The fight strips them bare—her fear of being left holding debts, his fear of mattering to someone who won't stay. The beat is the dark night of the relationship.

chapters.title: Margaret's Testimony
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper persuades Margaret Calloway to go on record about the forged Marchetti deed, trading her own silence for an old woman's courage. The beat is justice outside the law beginning as personal persuasion, not courtroom drama.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry Approaches
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. With the season ending, Theo packs for the mainland job he never refused outright, convinced Juniper will choose the settlement and a life without him. The beat is quiet resignation mistaken for peace.

chapters.title: Climax: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At the county hearing on the bank's practices, Juniper stands instead of signing, presenting the ledgers, the posthumous signature, and Margaret's testimony. Voss unravels publicly; the loan is voided pending investigation. The beat is the whole heart risked, and vindication that costs her composure but wins her future.

chapters.title: What She Should Have Said
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo learns of the hearing from the dock radio and realizes she fought alone because he taught her she'd leave. He runs for the pier as the last ferry loads. The beat is regret racing the tide.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper reaches the dock as the ferry casts off—and finds Theo didn't board; he's standing on the pier with his mother's deed and no terms left to negotiate. They speak plainly for the first time. The beat is surrender to belonging.

chapters.title: First Pressing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, epilogue-style. Spring: the vineyard's first independent pressing, Margaret planting roses on returned land, Theo's tools in the boathouse he's rebuilding. Juniper amends the old napkin contract to one clause: everything shared. The beat is earned sweetness—the vow kept.
